name: Military
scope: U.S. military / defense institution in operational military functions — Joint Staff, Services, Combatant Commands, DoD bodies. AARO credited only for its defense-institution functions.
excludes: The legislation that required AARO (Legislative); AARO's non-military executive functions (Government). Foreign military acts (International).
method: First-principles ladder, reality checked against the public record. Non-ontological: rungs measure institutional acts (an admission of custody, a capability to test evidence), never the existence of exotic material.
read: The base machinery works — reporting, preservation, fusion, analysis — but everything above stalls at in-progress, and the acts that would mean admitting what is held stay untaken. A working intake with a closed top.
summary: Only one rung is settled: UAP are officially recognized as reportable military events. Everything above is a capability in progress — evidence capture, fusion, analytic resolution, doctrine, forensics, allied interoperability and public release all exist in some form but are demonstrably incomplete — and the top acts (custody admission, systematic command-owned accountability) have not been taken.
sourcingQuality: Strong — first-party U.S. government records (defense.gov, media.defense.gov, aaro.mil).

rungs.title: Operational recognition & reportability
rungs.oneLiner: UAP formally reportable across Services. e.g. Joint Staff GENADMIN, May 2023.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Minimum positive act — UAP become reportable military events, entering reporting systems rather than being informal/stigmatized.
rungs.statusRationale: UAP are formally reportable across Services and Commands. Discrete, settled act.

sources.label: Joint Staff GENADMIN, UAP Reporting and Material Disposition, May 2023 (FOIA 23-F-1423)

rungs.title: Standardized capture & evidence preservation
rungs.oneLiner: Templates, deadlines, chain of custody exist. Partial: sensor data still insufficient (FY2025).
rungs.firstPrinciples: A legitimate report without standardized data is just an anecdote. This rung makes observations usable and resistant to loss/alteration.
rungs.statusRationale: The standard exists, but AARO's FY2025 report states sensor data remains insufficient/late — capture doesn't yet reliably produce usable data.

sources.label: May 2023 Joint Staff GENADMIN (templates, deadlines, chain of custody)

rungs.title: Joint ownership & cross-service fusion
rungs.oneLiner: A named DoD body fuses reporting. Partial: DoD IG found fragmentation.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Standardized evidence can stay fragmented; a named body creates institutional memory and common prioritization.
rungs.statusRationale: A named fusion body exists, but the DoD Inspector General found fragmentation and no coordinated, overarching approach — fusion is not mature.

sources.label: DoD Inspector General — fragmentation, no coordinated approach

rungs.title: Repeatable analytic resolution
rungs.oneLiner: Cases resolved with documented methods. Partial: hard residual, method not fully auditable.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A fusion office can merely accumulate; this rung requires a functioning decision process with confidence judgments and a retained residual.
rungs.statusRationale: The process exists and resolves hundreds of cases with published methods, but can still gain substantially in volume, speed, precision, reproducibility and handling of the hard residual, and methods are not fully auditable.

sources.label: AARO FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report; GoFast Case Resolution Methodology, Feb 2025

rungs.title: Operational response doctrine
rungs.oneLiner: Engagement acknowledged. Partial: full trained doctrine/ROE not publicly demonstrated.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Analysis describes what happened; doctrine commits units to what they must do, allocating responsibility and risk.
rungs.statusRationale: An architecture is acknowledged and still being implemented (a classified Feb 2025 Joint Staff GENADMIN), but intercept/response rules are not publicly demonstrated.

sources.label: AARO FY2025 report (ongoing implementation of a classified Feb 2025 GENADMIN)

rungs.title: Independent scientific & forensic exploitation
rungs.oneLiner: Labs analyzed claimed specimens (ORNL). Partial: no standing pathway for verified evidence.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Operational analysis serves threat attribution; forensic exploitation applies specialized, replicable methods outside the originating unit.
rungs.statusRationale: Capability to commission credible external testing of claimed samples exists; a standing pathway for verified incident-derived evidence does not.

sources.label: ORNL Synopsis: Analysis of a Metallic Specimen, 10 July 2024

rungs.title: Allied operational interoperability
rungs.oneLiner: Foreign-partner reporting pathways exist. Partial: no verified NATO/Five Eyes protocol.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Domestic jointness binds one institution's components; allied interoperability exposes reporting standards to external governments and needs reciprocal arrangements.
rungs.statusRationale: Verified allied/partner reporting pathways and exchange exist, but no binding NATO/Five Eyes/bilateral protocol is named — activity, not a verified architecture.

sources.label: May 2023 GENADMIN (allied/partner/host-nation reporting pathways, Five Eyes equities)

rungs.title: Selective evidentiary transparency
rungs.oneLiner: Official releases happen. Partial: selective, redacted, no raw sensor data.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Internal/allied sharing stays controlled; public release is irreversible and exposes official uncertainty to outside criticism.
rungs.statusRationale: The step is taken (official public release of primary evidence exists), but it is not mature: selective, redacted, short clips without raw sensor data. A qualitative gap to proactive, complete release remains.

sources.label: DoD Statement on the Release of Historical Navy Videos, 27 April 2020

rungs.title: Acknowledged custody of materials & biologics
rungs.oneLiner: No official admission of held materials. Measures the admission, not the existence.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Measures the public admission of holding materials/biologics — the heaviest single act of transparency. Distinct from forensic capability: a lab can test an alleged sample without any custody ever being admitted.
rungs.statusRationale: No official public admission of held materials. Only sworn allegations exist.

rungs.title: Systematic, command-owned public accountability
rungs.oneLiner: No release presumption, no command-backed accountability, no audit right.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Selective publication is discretionary and can favor easy cases. This rung subjects disclosure decisions and unresolved cases to a durable, auditable, command-owned regime.
rungs.statusRationale: No public Service/Joint Staff/Command directive establishes a routine release presumption, command-backed first-hand accountability, or independent technical-scrutiny right. AARO cannot independently declassify.

sources.label: AARO and the Declassification Process, 2025 (origin-office controls release)

crossTrackNotes: AARO is credited here only for military-institution functions (reporting, fusion, analysis, military-origin release). The legislation requiring AARO is Legislative; its non-military executive functions are Government.
